summary: Groechenig, Wyss and Ziegler give a second proof of Ngô's Geometric Stabilisation Theorem — the statement relating the κ-isotypic cohomology of the Hitchin fibres of a quasi-split reductive group scheme G over a curve to the stable cohomology of the Hitchin fibres of its endoscopy groups, and hence the Fundamental Lemma — which uses neither the Decomposition Theorem nor Ngô's Support Theorem. Instead they develop p-adic integration on coarse moduli spaces of smooth tame Deligne–Mumford stacks: a canonical measure vol_M on M(O_F)^♮, a specialisation map to the twisted inertia stack I_µ̂M(k), and the formula vol_M(e^{-1}(x, α)) = q^{-w(x,α)}/|Aut(x, α)| that turns volumes into weighted point counts. Two geometric results carry the proof: the twisted inertia stack of the anisotropic Higgs stack is the disjoint union of the Higgs stacks of the coendoscopic groups (Theorems 5.14 and 5.23), and the Pryms of G and of its Langlands dual Ĝ are dual Beilinson 1-motives in the quasi-split case (Theorem 4.28, proved by co-descent in Appendix A). Comparing the two p-adic integrals fibrewise over the Hitchin base, using Tate duality for abelian varieties over a local field and the identification of the integrand with the Hasse invariant of a gerbe, gives a character-sum identity (Theorem 6.11) from which geometric stabilisation and Waldspurger's non-standard fundamental lemma follow by Fourier inversion. The atlas plans the two main theorems, but only along Ngô's route: ET.2b of Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison plans the Hitchin geometry, the support theorem and the endoscopic comparison, and ET.3 derives the fundamental lemma from it. Nothing in the atlas plans p-adic integration on stacks, twisted inertia stacks, gerbes and the Hasse invariant on them, coendoscopic data, Beilinson 1-motives or duality of Pryms; nor does anything own Weil's canonical measure, Tate duality for abelian varieties over a local field, or the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula for stacks.

items.name: Geometric Stabilisation Theorem
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Corollary 6.18 (k a finite field with q elements, X/k a smooth projective curve with a rational point ∞, G/X a quasi-split reductive group scheme obtained from a split pinned G/k and an Out(G)-torsor ρ, D a line bundle on X of even degree d ≥ 2g−2 with A^♦ ≠ ∅, |Θ ⋉ W| invertible on X, and E = (κ, ρ_κ, ρ_κ → ρ) a coendoscopic datum for the Langlands dual Ĝ whose torsor ρ_{κ,∞} splits): for every a ∈ Ã_H(k) one has #^{κ_a} M̄_{G,a}(k) = q^{r^G_H(D)} · #^stab M̄_{H,a}(k), where r^G_H(D) = ½(dim M̃_G − dim M̃_H) and #^κ Y(k) = Tr(Fr, H*_c(Y, Q̄_ℓ)^κ) is the κ-isotypic point count.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Theorem 1.1, p. 3 (proved as Corollary 6.18, p. 41)
items.note: This is Ngô's Theorem 6.4.2 ([Ngô10]). ET.2b plans exactly this comparison of κ-isotypic direct images along Ngô's route (weak abelian fibrations, δ-stratification, the support theorem); the paper proves the same statement without the Decomposition or Support Theorem, which is why its machinery is routed to a Part II rather than into ET.2b.

items.name: Cohomology of a Higgs stack and of its rigidification agree
items.statement: Since M_{G,a} is a gerbe over M̄_{G,a} banded by a finite étale group scheme, the Q̄_ℓ-adic cohomology groups of M_{G,a} and of M̄_{G,a} are canonically isomorphic; in particular the two stacks have the same number of k-rational points over a finite field k.
items.note: Lets the theorem be stated for Ngô's stacks M_G and proved for the rigidifications M̄_G.

items.name: Geometric non-standard fundamental lemma for dual groups
items.statement: For every a ∈ Ã_G(k) ≅ Ã_Ĝ(k) one has #^stab M̃_{G,a}(k) = #^stab M̃_{Ĝ,a}(k): the stable parts of the point counts of the Hitchin fibres of G and of its Langlands dual Ĝ agree.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Theorem 1.3, p. 3 (proved as Corollary 6.17, p. 40)
items.note: This is Ngô's Theorem 8.8.2, the geometric form of Waldspurger's non-standard fundamental lemma [Wal08]. ET.3 plans the ordinary and the non-standard variant with their root-datum isogeny conditions; the geometric statement here is the input ET.3 consumes.

items.name: Weil's canonical measure and point counts
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field with ring of integers O_F and residue field k = F_q, and let X/O_F be a smooth scheme of relative dimension d with specialisation map e : X(O_F) → X(k). There exists a canonical measure µ_can on X(O_F) such that for every k-rational point x ∈ X(k) one has vol(e^{-1}(x)) = q^{-d}; in particular vol(X(O_F)) = |X(k)| · q^{-d}.
items.note: The prototype of the whole method: a p-adic volume computes a point count. No layer of the atlas constructs Weil's measure; LD.2 plans p-adic definable measures and Igusa-type integrals, which is where this belongs.

items.name: Volume of the fibres of the specialisation map (stacky Weil formula)
items.statement: Let M/O_F be a smooth tame Deligne–Mumford stack as in Situation 2.6(b), with coarse moduli space M, maximal open V ⊂ M over which M → M is an isomorphism, M(O_F)^♮ = M(O_F) ∩ V(F) and specialisation map e : M(O_F)^♮ → [I_µ̂M(k)]. For every x ∈ I_µ̂M(k) one has vol_M(e^{-1}(x)) = q^{-w(x)} / |Aut_{I_µ̂M(k)}(x)|, where w is the weight function of Definition 2.20; in particular vol(M(O_F)^♮) = #_w I_µ̂M(k), the weighted count taking both automorphisms and the weight into account.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Theorem 1.5, p. 4 (= Theorem 2.21, p. 13)
items.note: The engine of the paper. Known in motivic integration ([DL02], [Yas06]); the authors state explicitly that they do not know how to deduce it formally from those results.

items.name: Measure attached to an r-fold top-degree form on an F-analytic manifold
items.statement: Let X be an n-dimensional analytic manifold over a non-archimedean local field F with normalised Haar measure µ_{F^n} (µ_{F^n}(O_F^n) = 1), and let ω be a global section of (Ω^n_X)^{⊗r}. For a compact open chart U ↪ F^n and an analytic function f : U → F with ω|_U = f(x)(dx_1 ∧ … ∧ dx_n)^{⊗r}, set µ_ω(U) = ∫_U |f|^{1/r} dµ_{F^n}; this extends to a measure on X.
items.note: Analytic manifolds and differential forms over F are defined as over the reals, following [Igu00]; the extension to a measure follows [Yas17, 3.2].

items.name: Haar measure on F^n
items.statement: F^n is a locally compact abelian group, so it carries a left-invariant Haar measure, unique up to a positive scalar; µ_{F^n} is normalised by µ_{F^n}(O_F^n) = 1.
items.note: Mathlib constructs, for a positive compact K₀ of a locally compact group, a left-invariant measure haarMeasure K₀ normalised by haarMeasure K₀ K₀ = 1, and proves that every σ-finite left-invariant measure on a second-countable locally compact group is a scalar multiple of it; the additive forms used here (F^n with K₀ = O_F^n) are the `to_additive` images of the cited declarations. Local compactness of a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field is Mathlib's `Valued.integer` API in Topology/Algebra/Valued/LocallyCompact.lean.

items.name: Positive-codimension subspaces are null
items.statement: For X a geometrically reduced algebraic space of finite type over O_F and a closed algebraic subspace Y ⊂ X of positive codimension, µ_ω(Y(O_F)) = 0.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Proposition 2.1(a), p. 6 ([Yas17, Lemma 4.3, Theorem 4.8])
items.note: Used throughout to discard the non-generic loci: M(O_F) \ M(O_F)^♮ and U_a(O) \ U_a(O)^♭.

items.name: Change of variables under a generically free finite étale quotient
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of geometrically reduced algebraic spaces of finite type over O_F. Assume Y carries a generically stabiliser-free action of a finite étale group scheme Γ over O_F, that f is Γ-invariant and that the induced morphism Y/Γ → X is birational. Then for every open Γ-invariant A ⊂ Y(O_F) and every section ω of (Ω^top_X)^{⊗r} one has (1/|Γ(F)|) ∫_A |f^*ω|^{1/r} = ∫_{f(A)} |ω|^{1/r}.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Proposition 2.1(b), p. 6 ([Yas17, Lemma 4.3, Theorem 4.8])
items.note: The authors note that the literature's assumption that X be a scheme is superfluous: the case of algebraic spaces is identical.

items.name: Isogeny invariance of the integral of a top form
items.statement: Let A and B be dual abelian varieties over F and φ : A → B an isogeny of degree coprime to p. Then for every ω ∈ H^0(B, Ω^top_{B/F}) one has ∫_{A(F)} |φ^*ω| = ∫_{B(F)} |ω|.
items.note: The one place where duality of abelian varieties enters the measure comparison; it is what makes the two Hitchin systems have equal volumes (Lemma 6.15).

items.name: Relative top forms and the Fubini decomposition
items.statement: For a smooth morphism π : M^♦ → A^♦ of smooth O_F-schemes the short exact sequence 0 → π^*Ω^1_{A^♦/O_F} → Ω^1_{M^♦/O_F} → Ω^1_{M^♦/A^♦} → 0 induces an isomorphism π^*Ω^top_{A^♦/O_F} ⊗ Ω^top_{M^♦/A^♦} ≅ Ω^top_{M^♦/O_F}, η ⊗ φ ↦ η ∧ φ, and hence a fibrewise (Fubini) expression of the measure attached to a top form as an integral over A(O_F)^♭ = A(O_F) ∩ A^♦(F) of the fibrewise integrals.
items.note: The Fubini theorem used is [Igu00, Theorem 7.6.1] for smooth morphisms of p-adic manifolds.

items.name: The double integral computing a singular fibre: π(x,y) = xy
items.statement: For π : A^2_{O_F} → A^1_{O_F}, (x,y) ↦ xy, one has (A^1_{O_F})^♦ = G_{m,O_F}; for a ∈ A^1(O_F) ∩ G_m(F) = O_F \ {0} projection to x gives an isomorphism of F-analytic manifolds π^{-1}(a)(O_F) ≅ {x ∈ O_F : |x| ≥ |a|}, under which (dx ∧ dy)/da = (dx ∧ dy)/(y dx + x dy) = dx/x; evaluating the resulting double integral recovers |π^{-1}(0)(k)| = 2q − 1.
items.note: The worked example that shows how a p-adic integral sees a singular special fibre; an acceptance test for any formalisation of the method.

items.name: Point counts agree for dual abelian fibrations (the toy comparison)
items.statement: Let M_1, M_2 and A be smooth O_F-schemes with proper surjective morphisms π_i : M_i → A, and let M_i^reg be smooth group schemes over A with open immersions M_i^reg ↪ M_i, and A^♦ ⊂ A open dense, such that: (i) codim(M_i \ M_i^reg ⊂ M_i) ≥ 2; (ii) there is an isogeny ρ : (M_1^reg)° → (M_2^reg)° between the relative identity components of degree prime to p; (iii) the preimages M_i^♦ = M_i ×_A A^♦ are contained in M_i^reg and are dual abelian schemes over A^♦ for the resulting group structures. Then |M_{1,a}(k)| = |M_{2,a}(k)| for every a ∈ A(k).
items.note: The scheme-level model of Theorem 6.11: dual abelian fibrations have equal special-fibre point counts. The Hitchin systems of G and Ĝ satisfy (i)–(iii) only after the stacky refinement of Sections 2.3–2.4.

items.name: Coarse moduli space of a tame Deligne–Mumford stack over O_F
items.statement: For a smooth and tame Deligne–Mumford stack M/O_F, M/O_F denotes a coarse moduli space with canonical map Q : M → M (Keel–Mori), and V ⊂ M the maximal open subscheme for which Q^{-1}(V) → V is an isomorphism.
items.note: R09.5 plans coarse spaces for the finite-inertia presentations of its own programme; the Keel–Mori statement for tame DM stacks over a discrete valuation ring, and the locus V where the map is an isomorphism, are what this paper needs.

items.name: Zariski-locally a finite étale quotient stack
items.statement: M is Zariski-locally a finite étale quotient stack if there is a finite covering by Zariski-open substacks M = ∪_{i∈I} M_i with equivalences M_i = [U_i/Γ_i], where Γ_i is a finite étale group O_F-scheme, U_i a smooth O_F-scheme, the action of Γ_i on U_i is generically free and every orbit lies in an affine subset.
items.note: By Kresch ([Kre09, Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 5.2]) a smooth tame DM stack over a field with quasi-projective coarse space is of this form, with the Γ_i constant; this is how the hypothesis is verified for M̄^ani_G in Situation 6.1.

items.name: The p-adic manifold of generic O_F-points
items.statement: In the notation of Situation 2.6, M(O_F)^♮ := M(O_F) ∩ V(F).
items.note: The set on which the measure lives: O_F-points of the coarse space whose generic fibre lies in the locus where the stack is an algebraic space.

items.name: The canonical measure on the coarse space of a tame DM stack
items.statement: Let M/O_F be a smooth tame DM stack with coarse moduli space M/O_F which is Zariski-locally a finite étale quotient as in Situation 2.6. Then there is a unique Borel measure vol_M on M(O_F) such that (a) vol_M(M(O_F)) = vol_M(M(O_F)^♮), and (b) for an open subscheme W ⊂ M and a generating section ω of (Ω^top_M)^{⊗r}(Q^{-1}(W)) (that is, O_W · ω = (Ω^top_M)^{⊗r}), vol_M(A) = ∫_A |ω|^{1/r} for every Borel measurable A ⊂ W(O_F)^♮.
items.note: Its proof uses that ∫_A |ω|^{1/r} is independent of the chosen r-gauge form ω and of r, and that norms Nm_{U_i/M_i}(η_i) of generating top forms along the finite étale maps U_i → M_i provide the required gauge forms.

items.name: r-gauge forms and their independence
items.statement: If ω_1, ω_2 are generating sections of (Ω^top_M)^{⊗r_1}, (Ω^top_M)^{⊗r_2} on the same open, and r = d_1 r_1 = d_2 r_2, then ω_2^{⊗d_2} = f ω_1^{⊗d_1} for a unit f ∈ O_M(U)^×, so |f(x)| = 1 and |ω_1(x)|^{1/r_1} = |ω_2(x)|^{1/r_2} for all x ∈ U(O_F); and the norm Nm_{U_i/M_i}(η_i) of a generating top form along the finite étale π_i : U_i → M_i generates (Ω^top_{M_i})^{⊗ deg π_i}.
items.note: The technical heart of the existence of vol_M: gauge forms exist Zariski-locally on the coarse space only after passing to a tensor power.

items.name: The twisted inertia stack
items.statement: For a stack X over Spec(k), the twisted inertia stack is the X-stack I_µ̂X = colim_n Hom(Bµ_n, X) → X.
items.note: Twisting refers to the µ_n-gerbes Bµ_n rather than to the constant group Z/n: this is the form of the inertia stack that sees the tame ramification of a local field.

items.name: Rational points of a twisted inertia stack: the groupoid description
items.statement: Let X/F_q be a stack whose diagonal is of finite presentation, and for a geometric point x ∈ X(F_q) let φ : Aut_{X(F̄_q)}(x) → Aut_{X(F̄_q)}(x) be the automorphism induced by the Frobenius φ ∈ Gal(F̄_q/F_q). Then there is an equivalence of groupoids I_µ̂X(F_q) ≃ {(x, α) : x ∈ X(F_q), α ∈ Hom_cts(µ̂(F̄_q), Aut_{X(F̄_q)}(x)), α ∘ φ = φ ∘ α}.
items.note: Makes the twisted inertia stack computable over a finite field.

items.name: Rational points of a twisted inertia stack: after a choice of generator
items.statement: With ξ a profinite generator of µ̂(F̄_q), sending (x, α) to (x, α(ξ)) gives an equivalence of groupoids [ξ] : I_µ̂X(F_q) ≃ {(x, α) ∈ IX(F̄_q) : x ∈ X(F_q) and φ^*α = α^q}.
items.note: The comparison with the ordinary inertia stack; the q-th power condition is the twist.

items.name: Automorphisms of a point of the twisted inertia stack
items.statement: For (x, α) ∈ I_µ̂X(F_q) as in Lemma 2.10(b) one has Aut_{I_µ̂X(F_q)}(x, α) = {β ∈ Aut_{X(F_q)}(x) : α ∘ β = β ∘ α}.
items.note: The centraliser that appears in the denominator of Theorem 2.21.

items.name: The µ_N-action on Spec(O_L) and Spec(L) as a µ_N-torsor
items.statement: Let L/F be a finite totally ramified extension of degree N with uniformiser π. For every O_F-algebra R and ζ ∈ µ_N(R) there is a unique automorphism of O_L ⊗_F R = R[π] fixing R and sending π to ζπ; this defines an action of µ_N on Spec(O_L) relative to Spec(O_F), independent of the choice of uniformiser, and endows Spec(L) with the structure of a µ_N-torsor over Spec(F).
items.note: Tame totally ramified extensions of a local field are planned in the Tau Ceti roadmap LocalFieldsRamification (Layer 3), but their µ_N-torsor structure is not.

items.name: Normalisation of a tame DM stack over O_F with generic fibre Spec F
items.statement: Let M be a tame DM stack over O_F such that (i) the diagonal M → M ×_{O_F} M is finite, (ii) M → Spec(O_F) is the coarse moduli space of M, and (iii) the generic fibre M_F equals Spec(F). Let M̃ be the normalisation of M. Then for some totally ramified finite extension F ⊂ L of degree N there is an isomorphism [Spec(O_L)/µ_N] ≅ M̃, unique up to isomorphism for a given L; the induced morphism [Spec(k_F)/µ_N] = [Spec(k_L)/µ_N] ≅ M̃_{k_F} on special fibres is independent of L up to isomorphism.
items.note: The local classification that produces the point of the twisted inertia stack; normalisation of a stack is taken in the sense of [AB17, Appendix A].

items.name: The specialisation map e : M(O_F)^♮ → [I_µ̂M(k)]
items.statement: For M a tame stack over Spec(O_F) with coarse moduli space M and x ∈ M(O_F)^♮, the pullback M_x = M ×_M Spec(O_F) satisfies conditions (ii) and (iii) of Proposition 2.12 (using that coarse moduli of tame stacks commute with base change, [AOV08, 3.3]); Proposition 2.12 then gives a morphism [Spec(k)/µ_N] → M̃_k → M_k and hence a point e(x) ∈ I_µ̂M(k), well defined up to isomorphism.
items.note: This is the map whose fibres Theorem 2.21 measures.

items.name: Torsors under a finite étale group scheme over a local field
items.statement: For Γ a finite étale group O_F-scheme of order coprime to p, H^1(F, Γ) denotes the pointed set of isomorphism classes of left Γ-torsors; for Γ constant there is a bijection of pointed sets H^1(F, Γ) ≅ Hom(Gal^{tr}(F), Γ)/Γ, where Gal^{tr}(F) is the tame quotient, topologically generated by a Frobenius lift and a generator of tame inertia.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Section 2.5, p. 11 ([Ser07, Section I.5])
items.note: Non-abelian Galois cohomology of finite group schemes over a local field: no layer of the atlas owns it (NC.3 plans non-abelian cohomology only in the unipotent/Selmer setting).

items.name: Unramified and strongly ramified torsors
items.statement: Let Q = Spec(∏_{i∈I} L_i) be a Γ-torsor. (i) [Q] = [x_β, 1] for some x_β ∈ Γ^un if and only if L_i/F is unramified for all i ∈ I (Q is then called unramified). (ii) [Q] = [1, x_γ] for some x_γ ∈ Γ^un if and only if L_i/F is totally ramified for at least one i; in that case any two totally ramified L_i, L_j are isomorphic and Γ(F) acts simply transitively on the corresponding connected components (Q is then called strongly ramified).
items.note: The dichotomy that turns a local point into a point of the twisted inertia stack.

items.name: Every torsor becomes strongly ramified after an unramified twist
items.statement: For every Γ-torsor Q there exists an unramified right Γ-torsor P such that the twist Q_P = P ×^Γ Q is a strongly ramified Γ_P-torsor, where Γ_P is the inner form of Γ defined by P.
items.note: Used to reduce Constructions 2.17–2.19 to the strongly ramified case.

items.name: The inertia subgroup of a strongly ramified torsor
items.statement: For Q a strongly ramified Γ-torsor and Spec(L) ⊂ Q a totally ramified connected component, I_Q ⊂ Γ denotes the stabiliser of Spec(L); it is well defined up to conjugation by Γ(F), and Spec(L) is an I_Q-torsor.
items.note: The group that becomes the automorphism group of the specialised point.

items.name: The inertia subgroup is canonically µ_N
items.statement: For a strongly ramified Γ-torsor Q there is a canonical isomorphism µ_N ≅ I_Q, where N = [L : F].
items.note: Canonicity here is what makes the specialisation map well defined.

items.name: The stack X_{Γ,Q} = [Q_O/Γ] and the closed immersion Bµ_N ↪ X_{Γ,Q}
items.statement: For a Γ-torsor Q over F let Q_O be the normalisation of Spec O_F in Q; by the valuative criterion the Γ-action extends uniquely, giving a smooth tame DM O_F-stack X_{Γ,Q} = [Q_O/Γ] containing j : Spec F = [Q/Γ] as a dense open. For every unramified right Γ-torsor P there is a canonical equivalence X_{Γ,Q} ≅ X_{Γ_P,Q_P}; choosing P with Q_P strongly ramified identifies the special fibre with B_k I_{Q_P} and yields a closed immersion B_kµ_N ↪ X_{Γ,Q}.
items.note: The closed immersion is not unique; Remark 3.8 shows that the induced map on Brauer groups is independent of the choice.

items.name: The specialisation map for a finite étale quotient stack
items.statement: For M = [U/Γ] a tame finite étale quotient stack with U a smooth O_F-scheme and x ∈ M(O_F)^♮, the pullback Spec(F) ×_M U is a Γ-torsor Q over F; applying the valuative criterion to U → U/Γ and the discrete valuation rings O_{L_i} with Q_O = Spec(∏_i O_{L_i}) gives a Γ-equivariant morphism Q_O → U, hence X_{Γ,Q} → M and, through (14), a morphism B_kµ_N → M whose class in [I_µ̂M(k)] is e(x).
items.note: The explicit form of Construction 2.13 used in every computation.

items.name: The fibres of the specialisation map
items.statement: For M = [U/Γ] and (x, α) ∈ I_µ̂M(k) as in Lemma 2.10(b), after twisting by a suitable unramified torsor one may assume x lies in the image of U(k) → M(k) and identify α with an element of Γ(k̄), giving an inclusion µ_N ↪ Γ with N = ord(α). With L = F(π^{1/N}) the tame totally ramified extension and U(O_L)^{µ_N}_x the set of µ_N-equivariant morphisms Spec(O_L) → U specialising to x, the quotient morphism induces a surjection U(O_L)^{µ_N}_x ↠ e^{-1}(x, α).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Construction 2.19, p. 13 (equation (15)); after [DL02, Section 2]
items.note: This surjection is what reduces Theorem 2.21 to a computation on U.

items.name: The weight of a µ̂-action and of a point of the twisted inertia stack
items.statement: (a) For (χ_1, …, χ_r) ∈ (Q/Z)^r set w(χ_1, …, χ_r) = Σ_{i=1}^r c_i, where c_i ∈ Q is the unique rational representative of χ_i with 0 < c_i ≤ 1. (b) For a k-vector space V with an algebraic action a : µ̂ → µ_N → Aut(V) and character decomposition V_k̄ ≅ ⊕_i V_k̄(χ_i), w(a) = w(χ_1, …, χ_r). (c) For (x, a) ∈ I_µ̂M(k) with M a smooth DM stack over k, w(x, a) is the weight of the induced µ̂-action on the tangent space T_xM.
items.note: Agrees through Lemma 2.10 with the usual weight defined on the untwisted inertia stack after fixing a primitive root of unity ([GWZ17, Definition 2.2]).

items.name: The stacky Weil formula
items.statement: Let M/O_F be a DM stack as in Situation 2.6(b). For (x, α) ∈ I_µ̂M(k) one has vol_M(e^{-1}(x, α)) = q^{-w(x,α)} / |Aut_{I_µ̂M(k)}(x, α)|.
items.note: The generalisation of Weil's Theorem 1.4 to tame quotient singularities; every point count in the paper is read off from it.

items.name: The linear model computation
items.statement: Let M = [A^n/µ_N] with µ_N acting linearly and non-trivially on A^n over O_F, let ξ ∈ µ_N(F) = µ_N(F_q) be a primitive N-th root of unity and 0 ∈ A^n the origin. Then (0, ξ) defines an element of I_µ̂M(F_q) and vol_M(e^{-1}(0, ξ)) = q^{-w(0,ξ)} / |µ_N(F)|.
items.note: The local computation from which Theorem 2.21 is deduced; the natural acceptance test.

items.name: Gerbes banded by an abelian group and their classification
items.statement: For X a stack and A an abelian sheaf, an A-gerbe on X is a stack over X which is locally non-empty and locally connected with band A; by Giraud's theorem the set of equivalence classes of A-gerbes on X is in natural bijection with the Čech cohomology group Ȟ²_ét(X, A). Unless stated otherwise 'gerbe' means G_m-gerbe, classified by Ȟ²_ét(X, G_m).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Lemma 3.2 and the conventions around it, p. 16
items.note: R09.4 plans algebraic stacks in the class this programme needs; Giraud's classification of gerbes by degree-two cohomology is the stack-theoretic input this paper adds to it.

items.name: Čech and derived degree-two cohomology agree
items.statement: If X is a scheme quasi-projective over an affine scheme, then Ȟ²_ét(X, G_m) = H²_ét(X, G_m).
items.note: No roadmap owns the Čech-to-derived comparison for schemes; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0 plans it only on analytic adic étale sites, which is a different statement.

items.name: The Hasse invariant of a local field
items.statement: For a non-archimedean local field F there is an isomorphism inv : H²_ét(F, G_m) → Q/Z, the Hasse invariant.
items.note: This is the local invariant map of local class field theory; the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap plans the Brauer group, the local invariant and local duality in its Layer 5.

items.name: Degree-two cohomology of Bµ_N over a field
items.statement: Let k be a field and N invertible in k. Then there is an equivalence f : H²_ét(B_kµ_N, G_m) ≅ Z/NZ, and for N' = dN with d coprime to p the diagram relating H²_ét(B_kµ_N, G_m) ≅ Z/NZ and H²_ét(B_kµ_{dN}, G_m) ≅ Z/dNZ commutes, the map on the right being multiplication by d, i.e. the inclusion (1/N)Z/Z ⊂ (1/dN)Z/Z ⊂ Q/Z.
items.note: The compatibility is what makes Definition 3.6 independent of N and lands the invariant in Q/Z.

items.name: Vanishing over an algebraically closed field
items.statement: H²_ét(B_k̄µ_N, G_m) = 0 for k̄ algebraically closed.
items.note: The geometric input of Lemma 3.4: the whole of H²(B_kµ_N, G_m) is arithmetic.

items.name: The invariant function f_α of a gerbe on a stack over a finite field
items.statement: Let k be a finite field, M/Spec k an algebraic stack and α a G_m-gerbe on M. Define f_α : I_µ̂M(k) → Q/Z by sending a k-rational point y : B_kµ_N → M of I_µ̂M to the invariant of y^*α ∈ H²_ét(B_kµ_N, G_m) ≅ Z/NZ = (1/N)Z/Z ⊂ Q/Z of Lemma 3.4.
items.note: The combinatorial shadow of the Hasse invariant on the twisted inertia stack.

items.name: The Hasse invariant is computed by the specialisation map
items.statement: Let F be a local field and M/O_F a smooth tame DM stack with coarse moduli space M/O_F as in Situation 2.6(b), and let α be a G_m-gerbe on M. For every x ∈ M(O_F)^♮ one has inv(x_F^*α) = f_α(e(x)), where x_F : Spec F → M is the induced map.
items.note: The bridge between arithmetic (Brauer classes over F) and geometry (the twisted inertia stack over k); it is what makes the character χ_s in Theorem 6.11 a p-adic integrand.

items.name: Independence of the closed immersion on Brauer groups
items.statement: For Q strongly ramified there is a (non-canonical) closed immersion of stacks i : B_kµ_N ↪ X_{Γ,Q} inducing on stabiliser groups the canonical inclusion µ_N ⊂ Γ, and the induced morphism Br(X_{Γ,Q}) → Br(B_kµ_N) is independent of the choices.
items.note: Makes Definition 3.9 well posed.

items.name: The invariant f_{Γ,Q} of a Brauer class on X_{Γ,Q}
items.statement: For Q strongly ramified, f_{Γ,Q} : H²_ét(X_{Γ,Q}, G_m) → Q/Z is the composition H²_ét(X_{Γ,Q}, G_m) →^{i^*} H²_ét(B_k I_Q, G_m) = H²_ét(B_kµ_N, G_m) = (1/N)Z/Z ⊂ Q/Z.
items.note: The local avatar of f_α.

items.name: f_{Γ,Q} computes the Hasse invariant of the restriction to the generic point
items.statement: For a strongly ramified Γ-torsor Q the diagram formed by j^* : H²_ét(X_{Γ,Q}, G_m) → H²_ét(F, G_m), the Hasse invariant inv and f_{Γ,Q} commutes.
items.note: The key step in the proof of Proposition 3.7.

items.name: The explicit cocycle for f_{Γ,Q}
items.statement: The 1-cocycle (c_{ij}) constructed from a trivialisation of the gerbe on the special fibre represents f_{Γ,Q}(α) ∈ H^1(k, µ_N^∨).
items.note: The computation behind Lemma 3.10; an explicit Čech-cocycle description of the invariant.

items.name: The gerbe attached to a finite-order line bundle
items.statement: Let M/O_F be a proper DM stack over the ring of integers of a local field F and L ∈ Pic(M) a G_m-torsor of finite order. The gerbe α_L ∈ H²_ét(M, G_m) is the element induced by the class in H^1(π_1(O_F), H^1_ét(M_{O_F^{un}}, G_m)) corresponding to the morphism Ẑ → H^1_ét(M, G_m) sending 1 to L.
items.note: The construction that turns the torsor T_G of Section 6.5 into a Brauer class.

items.name: The invariant of the gerbe of a character torsor
items.statement: With the notation of Definition 3.12 and the identification H^1_ét(B_kµ_N, G_m) ≅ µ_N^∨ = Z/NZ, χ ↔ L_χ, one has f(α_{L_χ}) = χ ∈ Z/NZ ⊂ Q/Z, where f is the invariant of Lemma 3.4.
items.note: Identifies the two ways of attaching a rational number to a point of the twisted inertia stack.

items.name: The Hasse invariant of α_L on generic O_F-points
items.statement: Let M be a proper tame DM stack as in Situation 2.6(b) and L ∈ Pic(M). For every x ∈ M(O_F)^♮ one has inv(x_F^*α_L) = χ_L(e(x)), where χ_L : I_µ̂M(k) → Q/Z sends y : B_kµ_N → M to the character of µ_N corresponding to y^*L ∈ Pic(B_kµ_N).
items.note: This identity, read as an identity of complex-valued functions through Q/Z ↪ C^×, is what is integrated in Section 6.3.

items.name: The embedding Q/Z ↪ C^×
items.statement: Q/Z is viewed inside C^× through λ ↦ e^{2πiλ}; all invariants are read as complex-valued functions through this embedding.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Corollary 3.14 and the paragraph after it, p. 19
items.note: Mathlib has the homomorphism AddCircle.toCircle : R/TZ → Circle, x ↦ exp(2πix/T), a group homomorphism by AddCircle.toCircle_add; with T = 1 it is λ ↦ e^{2πiλ} on R/Z, and the embedding the paper uses is its restriction to Q/Z ⊂ R/Z.

items.name: Pinning of a reductive group scheme
items.statement: A pinning of a reductive group scheme G over a scheme S is a triple (T, B, s) with T a maximal torus over S, B a Borel subgroup over S containing T and s a section of Lie B over S such that over some étale covering S' of S the groups T, B, G become constant, B admits root subgroups U_α for the roots α ∈ Φ^+ appearing in Lie B, and s decomposes as s = Σ_{α∈Φ^+} s_α for nowhere vanishing sections s_α of Lie U_α over S'. A pinning is split if T is split.
items.note: Pinned Chevalley–Demazure group schemes over Z are planned in the Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap (Layer 9); the relative version over a base scheme is the same definition.

items.name: Compatible pinnings of a reductive subgroup
items.statement: For H ⊂ G a closed reductive subgroup scheme, a pinning (T', B', s') of H is compatible with a pinning (T, B, s) of G if T' = T, B' ⊂ B, and over a suitable étale covering on which all groups become constant the summands satisfy s_α = s'_α for those roots α appearing in Lie B'.
items.note: The compatibility used to endow every coendoscopic group H_κ with a canonical pinning.

items.name: The sheaf of pinnings is a torsor under the adjoint group
items.statement: For a reductive group scheme G over S, the sheaf of pinnings of G is a torsor under G^ad.
items.note: A statement of SGA 3 about pinned reductive group schemes; the Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap plans the structure theory (Layer 7) and the pinned Chevalley–Demazure theory (Layer 9) that own it.

items.name: A pinning splits the outer-automorphism sequence
items.statement: For a reductive group scheme G over S with exact sequence of sheaves 1 → G^ad → Aut(G) → Out(G) → 1, the subsheaf of Aut(G) of automorphisms fixing a given pinning maps isomorphically onto Out(G); hence every pinning splits the sequence, and Out(G) is regarded as a subsheaf of Aut(G).
items.note: Also SGA 3 structure theory of pinned reductive group schemes, planned in ReductiveGroups Layers 7 and 9.

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of the compatible pinning of a subgroup
items.statement: Let S be a scheme, G a reductive group scheme over S, H ⊂ G a closed reductive subgroup scheme, and (T, B, s) a pinning of G with T ⊂ H. Then there is a unique pinning (T', B', s') of H compatible with (T, B, s).
items.note: Applied to the connected centralisers H_κ ⊂ G, which is how coendoscopic groups acquire canonical pinnings (Section 5.2).

items.name: Outer forms and quasi-split reductive group schemes
items.statement: An outer form of a pinned reductive group scheme G over S is a group scheme G → S together with an Out(G)-torsor ρ_G on S and an isomorphism G ≅ ρ_G ×^{Out(G)}_S G, which induces a pinning on G. A reductive group scheme over S is quasi-split if it admits a pinning; and a quasi-split G over S with a chosen pinning is isomorphic, compatibly with pinnings, to G ×^{Out(G)} ρ for a split pinned G/S and an Out(G)-torsor ρ.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Definitions 4.5, 4.6 and Lemma 4.7, p. 20
items.note: Quasi-split group schemes over a curve are the standing generality of the paper; no layer of the atlas constructs them (ET.2b speaks of reductive group schemes with descent under outer twists but does not develop the theory).

items.name: An outer-form torsor is trivialised by a finite étale cover
items.statement: Let X be a smooth projective curve over k and ρ an Out(G)-torsor on X. Then there exists a finite étale covering X' of X over which ρ becomes trivial.
items.note: This is what makes the co-descent argument of Appendix A applicable, and it also gives the reduction of ρ to a finite subgroup Θ ⊂ Out(G) over a field (Remark 4.11).

items.name: The Langlands dual of a split reductive group scheme
items.statement: For G/k reductive, Ĝ/k denotes the reductive group classified by the dual root datum.
items.note: The pinned dual group of a split reductive group scheme is planned in GeometricSatake's integral dual-group stage, which reconstructs it and identifies its root datum.

items.name: The Langlands dual of a quasi-split outer form
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism Out(Ĝ) = Out(G); for an outer form G of G over a k-scheme S given by an Out(G)-torsor ρ, the Langlands dual Ĝ is the quasi-split outer form of Ĝ given by ρ regarded as an Out(Ĝ)-torsor.
items.note: The duality of the paper is between the Hitchin systems of G and of this Ĝ; the outer-form version of the dual group is not planned anywhere.

items.name: The standing situation for Hitchin systems
items.statement: Situation 4.10: R a commutative ring; X_R/R a flat family of smooth projective curves with geometrically connected fibres; D a line bundle on X_R of even degree d; G a split reductive group scheme over Spec(R) with a split pinning (T, B, s) and G = G ×^{Out(G)} ρ a quasi-split form on X_R for an Out(G)-torsor ρ; g, g, t, t the Lie algebras of G, G, T, T; and a finite subgroup scheme Θ ↪ Out(G) such that |Θ ⋉ W| is invertible on X_R and ρ admits a Θ-reduction.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Situation 4.10 and Remark 4.11, pp. 20–21
items.note: The invertibility of |Θ ⋉ W| is the paper's good-characteristic hypothesis; it replaces Ngô's p > 2·(Coxeter number) only for the statements proved here.

items.name: G-Higgs bundles and their moduli stack
items.statement: A G-Higgs bundle with coefficients in D is a pair (E, θ) with E a G-torsor on X_R and θ a global section of ad(E) ⊗ D, where ad(E) = E ×^G_{X_R} g; M_G = M_G(X, D) is the stack sending an affine R-scheme S to the groupoid of G-Higgs bundles on X_S/S.
items.note: ET.2b plans the stack of G-bundles with Higgs fields twisted by a sufficiently positive divisor, with algebraicity and finite-type bounds.

items.name: The generic stabiliser and the rigidified Higgs stack
items.statement: The generic stabiliser group of M_G is the group scheme Z(X, G) obtained as the Weil restriction of Z(G) over X along the proper morphism X → Spec(R) (representable by [Ols06, Theorem 1.5]); M̄_G denotes the rigidification of M_G by this group scheme in the sense of [ACV03, Theorem 5.1.5].
items.note: Rigidification is exactly what makes M̄_G a DM stack to which the p-adic integration of Section 2 applies; R09.5 plans coarse spaces and rigidification of automorphisms in its own setting, but not the rigidification of a Higgs stack by a Weil restriction of centres.

items.name: Higgs bundles as sections of [g_D/G]
items.statement: Let g_D = g ×^{G_m}_X D be the principal Lie algebra bundle obtained by twisting g/X with D, with the induced relative adjoint action of G. The datum of a G-Higgs bundle (E, θ) with coefficients in D is equivalent to a section of the morphism of X-stacks [g_D/G] → X.
items.note: The stacky reformulation on which the Hitchin map and the endoscopic morphisms µ_E are built; ET.2b plans the Chevalley quotient and Higgs stack in this form.

items.name: Chevalley base, Hitchin base and Hitchin map
items.statement: c = g/G is the Chevalley base, with induced affine space bundle c/X and G_m-action, and c_D = c ×^{G_m}_X D; A = A_G(X, D) is the affine scheme corresponding to H^0(X, c_D); the Hitchin map χ : M_G → A sends an S-family (E, θ) to the section of c_D defined by the composite X → [g_D/G] → c_D. For split G/X, A ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^m H^0(X, D^{⊗e_i}) with e_1, …, e_m the exponents ([Ngô10, 4.13]).
items.note: ET.2b plans the Chevalley quotient, the Hitchin base and the Hitchin map.

items.name: Cameral covers
items.statement: For a ∈ A(S) the cameral cover C_a → X ×_R S is the finite W-equivariant morphism in the cartesian diagram C_a → t_D over X ×_R S →^a c_D; C → X ×_R A denotes the universal cameral cover.
items.note: ET.2b plans cameral and spectral covers.

items.name: Strict Picard stacks
items.statement: A stack P with a strict symmetric monoidal structure ⊗ : P × P → P is a strict Picard stack if the induced monoid structure on the sheafification π_0^{sh}(P) of isomorphism classes is a group structure.
items.note: ET.2b plans the Picard stack acting on Hitchin fibres, but not the 2-categorical theory of strict Picard stacks that the duality statements of this paper are formulated in.

items.name: Regular centralisers and the abstract Prym
items.statement: J/[c/G_m] denotes the sheaf of regular centralisers ([Ngô10, 2.1]); for a ∈ A(S) = H^0(X_S, c_D) the induced commutative group scheme a^*J over X_S is again written J, and P = P_{G,X_S,D} denotes the stack of J-torsors.
items.note: ET.2b plans the regular-centraliser group scheme with descent under outer twists and the Picard stack it defines.

items.name: The action of the Prym on the Higgs stack
items.statement: For a Higgs bundle (E, θ) over S with Hitchin image a ∈ A(S) there is a natural morphism J → Aut(E, θ); for a J-torsor M the twist M ⊗ E = E ×^J_X M carries a canonical section of ad(E ⊗ M) ⊗ D, giving the Higgs bundle M ⊗ (E, θ) and the action of P on M_G relative to A ([Ngô10, 4.3.2]).
items.note: The Picard-stack action on Hitchin fibres planned by ET.2b.

items.name: Regular Higgs bundles
items.statement: A Higgs bundle (E, θ) is regular if its classifying section X → [g_D/G] factors through the open dense substack [g^reg_D/G]; similarly for S-families, giving the open substack M^reg.
items.note: The regular locus of the Hitchin system, planned with the Kostant section in ET.2b.

items.name: Kostant section and the torsor structure on the regular locus
items.statement: (i) To every square root D' of D (D'^{⊗2} ≅ D) one associates canonically a Kostant section ε^{D'} : A → M^reg; in particular M^reg is non-empty. (ii) The action of P on M^reg relative to A is a torsor structure, so every square root D' yields a trivialisation of torsors ε^{D'} : P ≅ M^reg.
items.note: ET.2b plans the Kostant section and the Picard-torsor structure on the regular locus.

items.name: Beilinson 1-motives
items.statement: A strict Picard stack P → S on a scheme S is a Beilinson 1-motive if there is a surjective étale covering S' → S such that P ×_S S' is equivalent to a product C ×_{S'} A ×_{S'} B_{S'}K with C and K finite étale group schemes over S' and A → S' a connected abelian scheme. The 2-category of Beilinson 1-motives carries a duality simultaneously extending duality of abelian varieties and Cartier duality of finite étale group schemes.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Definition 4.21 and the paragraph after it, p. 23
items.note: The category in which the Langlands duality of Pryms is stated; nothing in the atlas plans it (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli plans duality of abelian schemes only).

items.name: The smooth-cameral locus A^♦
items.statement: A^♦ ⊂ A is the open subset of geometric points a : Spec k̄ → A whose cameral cover C_a is smooth; M^♦, P^♦ etc. denote the pullbacks of M, P etc. to A^♦. For deg D > 2g the locus A^♦ is non-empty ([Ngô10, Proposition 4.7.1]).
items.note: Part of the Hitchin-base geometry planned in ET.2b; the paper's whole comparison happens over this locus, where the Prym is a family of abelian varieties.

items.name: The Prym over the smooth-cameral locus is a Beilinson 1-motive
items.statement: M^♦ ⊂ M^reg, and P^♦ is a Beilinson 1-motive ([Ngô10, Proposition 4.7.7]).
items.note: This is what allows Tate duality and the measure comparison to be applied fibrewise.

items.name: W-equivariant T-torsors with +-structure
items.statement: For a ∈ A(S) with cameral cover C_a and the maximal torus T ⊂ G of the pinning, with the natural actions act_1 : W ×_X T → T and act_2 : W ×_X C_a → C_a, a W-equivariant T-torsor is an object of the stack Bun^W_T(C_a) obtained from the W-action w(E) = (act_2(w^{-1})^*E) ×^{T,w}_{X×_R S} T on T-torsors on the small étale site of C_a; a +-structure on E is a family of isomorphisms c_α : (E|_{C_a^{s_α}}) ×^T G_m ≅ C_a^{s_α} × G_m for étale-local roots α ∈ Φ(U), compatible with the canonical isomorphisms can_{α,α̌} induced by the W-equivariant structure for coroots α̌ ∈ Φ^∨(U').
items.note: Donagi–Gaitsgory's description of J-torsors, extended from the split to the quasi-split case because it is étale-local on X.

items.name: Donagi–Gaitsgory: the Prym as W-equivariant T-torsors
items.statement: There is a canonical equivalence of strict Picard stacks Bun^{W,+}_T(C_a) ≅ P_a.
items.note: The concrete model of the Prym used to construct the Abel–Jacobi map and the duality.

items.name: The Abel–Jacobi map
items.statement: For S over Spec(R) let C_a^{sm} be the maximal open subset of C_a smooth over S. For an S-point (x, λ) ∈ C_a^{sm} ×_X X_*(T), the T-torsor O(λx) = O_{C_a}(x) ×^{λ,G_m} T carries a W-equivariant structure with +-structure (as in [CZ17, 3.4]); the resulting morphism C_a^{sm} ×_X X_*(T) → P_a ≅ Bun^{W,+}_T(C_a) is the Abel–Jacobi map.
items.note: The source of all the explicit points of the Prym used in Sections 6.4–6.5.

items.name: Langlands duality of Pryms for quasi-split groups
items.statement: Let X/k be a smooth projective curve over a field k and G/X a quasi-split reductive group scheme, i.e. an outer form of a split reductive G/k. If char(k) = 0 or |W| is not divisible by char(k), the morphism AJ^*_G : (P^♦_G)^∨ → P^♦_Ĝ is an equivalence of strict Picard stacks.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Theorem 4.28, p. 24 (= Corollary A.12; after [DP12], [CZ17])
items.note: Proved in Appendix A by co-descent from the split case; the assumption that k be algebraically closed in the cited sources is removed by faithfully flat descent. This is one of the two results the abstract of the paper advertises as new.

items.name: The rigidified Prym
items.statement: P̄ denotes the rigidification of P with respect to the abelian group Z(X, G) = H^0(X, Z(G)) ([ACV03, Theorem 5.1.5]); P̄ → A is an algebraic space with a relative group object structure, and its fibres are extensions of finite étale abelian group schemes by abelian varieties.
items.note: The group that acts on the rigidified Higgs stack M̄_G and whose duality drives the comparison.

items.name: The isogeny between the Pryms of G and of its dual
items.statement: There is an isomorphism of neutral connected components J° ≅ Ĵ° ([Ngô10, Proposition 2.4.7]); choosing N a multiple of the orders of π_0(J) and π_0(Ĵ), the N-th power maps factor through the identity components and give φ_N : J → Ĵ, hence an isogeny ρ : P̄_G → P̄_Ĝ. Over a field k of characteristic p one may take N coprime to p, because |π_0(J)| divides |Z(X, G)| ([Ngô10, Corollaire 2.3.2]) and Z(X, G) embeds into a torus, so its order is coprime to p.
items.note: The prime-to-p isogeny that Proposition 2.2 needs; the argument that N may be chosen coprime to p is exactly where the good-characteristic hypothesis is used.

items.name: The anisotropic locus
items.statement: A geometric point a ∈ A(k̄) is anisotropic if π_0(P̄_a) is finite and a lies in the open subset A^♥ of [Ngô10, 4.5] (reduced cameral cover); there is an open A^ani with this property ([Ngô10, 6.1]), and M^ani = M ×_A A^ani.
items.note: ET.2b plans the proper anisotropic quotient of the Hitchin system.

items.name: The anisotropic locus only depends on the root datum up to isogeny
items.statement: By [Ngô10, 4.10.5], a ∈ A^ani is equivalent to a ∈ A^♥ together with finiteness of T̂^{W_a}; hence A^ani_{G_1} = A^ani_{G_2} whenever G_1 and G_2 have isogenous root data, and in particular, under the identification A_G ≅ A_Ĝ, the open subsets A^ani_G and A^ani_Ĝ agree.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Definition 4.31 and Remark 4.32, p. 25
items.note: Needed for the two sides of Theorem 6.11 to be integrals over the same base.

items.name: The étale cover Ã → A and the stacks M̃_G
items.statement: For a fixed base point ∞ ∈ X(R), with c_{D,∞} the pullback of c_D along ∞ and ev_∞ : A → c_{D,∞} the evaluation map, Ã → A is the étale morphism defined by the cartesian square with t^{rs}_{D,∞} → c_{D,∞}; M̃_G = M_G ×_A Ã and M̃^ani_G = M^ani_G ×_A Ã ([Ngô10, 5.3.1]).
items.note: The base change that rigidifies the Hitchin fibres at ∞; all point counts in Section 6 are over Ã.

items.name: The embedding of automorphisms into the torus at infinity
items.statement: For S an R-scheme and (E, θ, ∞̃) ∈ M̃^ani_G(S) there is a canonical injective homomorphism Aut(E, θ) → T_∞(S) (identified with T after a choice of ∞_ρ ∈ ρ_∞(R)), constructed from the commuting diagram defining ∞̃ : S → t^{rs}_{D,∞}; by [Ngô10, 4.11.4] every automorphism γ of a Higgs bundle over A^ani has finite order r coprime to p.
items.note: This is what turns a point of the twisted inertia stack into a homomorphism κ : µ̂ → T, i.e. into endoscopic data.

items.name: From the Abel–Jacobi map to the component group
items.statement: Composing Ã → A^∞ → X × A with the Abel–Jacobi map gives a canonical morphism Ã → C^{sm} and hence Ã × X_*(T) = Ã × X_*(T_∞) → C^{sm} ×_X X_*(T) → P̄_G, and therefore Ã × X_*(T) → Ã ×_A P̄_G = P̃_G.
items.note: The explicit source of rational points of the Prym used to twist Hitchin fibres.

items.name: Surjectivity onto the component group of the Prym
items.statement: The induced map X_*(T) × Ã^ani → π_0(P̃^ani_G) is a surjection; in particular for every a ∈ Ã^ani(k) the finite group scheme π_0(P̃^ani_{G,a}) is constant.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Proposition 4.38, p. 26 (combining [Ngô10, Lemme 4.10.2] and [Ngô06, Corollaire 6.7])
items.note: ET.2b plans exact component-group actions for the Picard stack acting on Hitchin fibres.

items.name: Quotient stacks of twisted group actions
items.statement: Let S be a base algebraic space, A and B smooth group algebraic spaces over S and X an algebraic space over S with actions of A and B, with A acting on B by group automorphisms so that B ×_S X → X is A-equivariant. For an A-torsor ρ over S the twists X̄ = X ×^A ρ and B̄ = B ×^A ρ carry an action B̄ ×_S X̄ → X̄, the actions of B and A on X × ρ combine to an action of B ⋊ A, and the quotient morphism induces an isomorphism of quotient stacks [(X × ρ)/(B ⋊ A)] ≅ [X̄/B̄].
items.note: A general fact about quotient stacks; it is the bookkeeping device for every outer twist in Section 5, so it belongs with the stack foundations of R09.4 rather than in the Higgs theory.

items.name: Centralisers of a homomorphism µ̂ → T and their component groups
items.statement: For a homomorphism κ : µ̂ → T over Spec(k), the centraliser (G ⋊ Out(G))_κ has connected-étale sequence 1 → H_κ → (G ⋊ Out(G))_κ → π_0(κ) → 1 with H_κ the connected centraliser of κ in G; H_κ carries the unique pinning (T, B ∩ H_κ, s') compatible with that of G (Lemma 4.4), and π_0(κ) acts on H_κ and G through the natural homomorphisms o_G : π_0(κ) → Out(G) and o_H : π_0(κ) → Out(H_κ).
items.note: The group-theoretic source of coendoscopic data.

items.name: The homomorphism ι_κ : H_κ ⋊ π_0(κ) → G ⋊ π_0(κ)
items.statement: There is a canonical homomorphism ι_κ such that (i) its restriction to the normal subgroup H_κ is the inclusion H_κ ⊂ G, (ii) the induced morphism on the quotients π_0(κ) is the identity, and (iii) the inclusion H_κ ↪ G is equivariant with respect to ι_κ for the conjugation actions; it is constructed from ι̃_κ : H_κ ⋊ π̃_0(κ) → G ⋊ π̃_0(κ), hφ ↦ h g_φ φ, on the subgroup sheaf π̃_0(κ) ⊂ (G ⋊ Out(G))_κ of elements preserving the pinning of H_κ, which sits in 1 → Z(H_κ) → π̃_0(κ) → π_0(κ) → 1.
items.note: The comparison homomorphism that produces the morphism of Higgs stacks µ_E.

items.name: ι_κ identifies H_κ ⋊ π_0(κ) with the full centraliser
items.statement: The homomorphism ι_κ factors through (G ⋊ π_0(κ))_κ and, composed with (G ⋊ π_0(κ))_κ → (G ⋊ Out(G))_κ, gives an isomorphism H_κ ⋊ π_0(κ) → (G ⋊ Out(G))_κ whose restriction to π_0(κ) splits the quotient homomorphism (G ⋊ Out(G))_κ → π_0(κ).
items.note: The splitting that makes the coendoscopic group quasi-split.

items.name: Coendoscopic data
items.statement: A coendoscopic datum for G over k is a triple E = (κ, ρ_κ, ρ_κ → ρ) consisting of a homomorphism κ : µ̂ → T over Spec(k), a π_0(κ)-torsor ρ_κ over X and an o_G-equivariant morphism ρ_κ → ρ; κ is its type. One sets H_E = H_κ ×^{π_0(κ)} ρ_κ (π_0(κ) acting through o_H), a quasi-split group scheme, with maximal torus T_E = T ×^{π_0(κ)} ρ_κ, Lie algebra h_E, and the induced homomorphism γ_E : µ̂ → Z(H_E) over X.
items.note: The paper's own notion: the objects that classify the twisted inertia of the Hitchin stack. ET.0 plans classical endoscopic data, which are the duals of these.

items.name: Endoscopic data and endoscopy groups
items.statement: The Langlands dual Ĥ_E of a coendoscopic group H_E is an endoscopy group for Ĝ.
items.note: Endoscopic triples, ellipticity, relevant embeddings and endoscopic groups are planned in ET.0; Remark 5.5 is the dictionary between that notion and the coendoscopic data of this paper.

items.name: The morphism of Higgs stacks attached to a coendoscopic datum
items.statement: For E = (κ, ρ_κ, ρ_κ → ρ) there is a canonical morphism µ_E : [h_{E,D}/H_E] → [g_D/G], obtained from Construction 5.1's identifications [h_{E,D}/H_E] ≅ [(h_E × ρ_κ × D)/(H_κ ⋊ (π_0(κ) × G_m))] and [g_D/G] ≅ [(g × ρ_κ × D)/(G ⋊ (π_0(κ) × G_m))] and from ι_κ × id; passing to coarse moduli gives ν_E : c_E = h_{E,D}/H_E → c = g_D/G, which coincides with the morphism of [Ngô10, 1.9], and hence compatible morphisms ν_E : A_E → A and M_{H_E} → M_G.
items.note: The geometric transfer map along which the two sides of geometric stabilisation are compared.

items.name: The anisotropic locus is preserved by the endoscopic map
items.statement: For a coendoscopic datum E for G over k, ν_E^{-1}(A^ani) = A^ani_E.
items.note: Keeps the whole comparison inside the anisotropic (proper) part of the Hitchin system.

items.name: Compatibility at the marked point
items.statement: Let E = (κ, ρ_κ, ρ_κ → ρ) be a coendoscopic datum and ∞_{ρ_κ} ∈ ρ_κ(k) a point above ∞. Then ∞_{ρ_κ} induces identifications G_∞ ≅ G and H_{E,∞} ≅ H_κ compatible with the pinnings, and the induced isomorphism t_{E,∞} ≅ t ≅ t_∞ makes the square formed by t_{E,D,∞} ≅ t_{D,∞} and ν_E : c_{E,∞} → c_∞ commute.
items.note: Needed to lift ν_E to the étale covers Ã.

items.name: The spaces Ã^{G-∞}_E and the lifted map ν̃_E
items.statement: With A^∞ ⊂ A the locus of elements regular semisimple at ∞ and Ã the pullback of t^{rs}_{D,∞} → c_{D,∞} along A^∞ → c_{D,∞}, let A^{G-∞}_E be the preimage of A^∞ in A_E and Ã^{G-∞}_E its preimage in Ã_E; the point ∞_{ρ_κ} induces ν̃_E : Ã^{G-∞}_E → Ã compatible with ν_E : A_E → A.
items.note: The base over which the twisted inertia stack is described.

items.name: From an automorphism of a Higgs bundle to a coendoscopic datum
items.statement: Given ∞_ρ ∈ ρ_∞(k), κ : µ̂ → T and an object (E, θ, ∞̃) of M̃^{∞,ani}_G(S) together with γ : µ̂ → Aut(E, θ) whose image under Construction 4.36 is κ: writing (E, θ) as a G ⋊ (π_0(κ) × G_m)-torsor Ẽ with equivariant θ̃ : Ẽ → g × ρ_κ × D, the automorphism γ becomes an automorphism of Ẽ stabilising θ̃; after fixing a section over an étale covering X' of X × S it is a homomorphism µ̂_{X'} → (G ⋊ (π_0(κ) × G_m))_{X'}, well defined up to conjugation, which factors through G because π_0(κ) × G_m acts without fixed points on g × ρ_κ × D.
items.note: The inverse construction to µ_E, and the reason the inertia of M̃_G is endoscopic.

items.name: Local conjugacy of the two homomorphisms
items.statement: The homomorphisms γ, κ : µ̂_{X'} → G_{X'} of Construction 5.10 are conjugate étale-locally over X'.
items.note: This is what produces the torsor ρ_κ out of γ.

items.name: The datum attached to a point of the inertia stack is coendoscopic
items.statement: For S = Spec(k) the datum (κ, ρ_κ, ρ_κ → ρ) of Construction 5.10 is a coendoscopic datum E for G over k, and the sheaf F̃ corresponds under Construction 5.1 to an H_E-Higgs bundle F over Spec(k) mapping to the point ((E, θ), γ) of IM(k) under µ_E.
items.note: The essential surjectivity half of Theorem 5.14.

items.name: Coendoscopic data occurring on the twisted inertia stack
items.statement: A coendoscopic datum E for G over k occurs on I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k) if there is a point of I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k) whose associated coendoscopic datum (Proposition 5.12) equals E.
items.note: Indexes the disjoint union in Theorem 5.14.

items.name: The twisted inertia stack of the anisotropic Hitchin stack is endoscopic
items.statement: For ∞_ρ ∈ ρ_∞(k) and points ∞_{ρ_κ} ∈ ρ_{κ,∞}(k) mapping to ∞_ρ for every coendoscopic datum E for G over k occurring on I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k), the resulting morphism of groupoids µ̃_E : ⊔_E M̃^{G-∞,ani}_{H_E}(k) → I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k) is an equivalence.
items.note: The second result the abstract advertises: a description of the inertia stack of the anisotropic Higgs moduli stack in terms of endoscopic data. It is the geometric input that replaces the support theorem.

items.name: Finiteness of the occurring coendoscopic data
items.statement: Only finitely many coendoscopic data for G over k̄ occur on I_µ̂M̃^ani_{G,k̄}; hence for k finite the points ∞_ρ and ∞_{ρ_κ} of Theorem 5.14 may always be chosen after replacing k by a finite extension.
items.note: Uses Construction 4.36, Construction 5.10 and finite type of I_µ̂M̃^ani_G.

items.name: Compatibility of µ_E with the evaluation at infinity
items.statement: The diagram formed by X → [h_D/H] →^{µ_E} [g_D/G], the coarse maps h_D/H →^{ν_E} g_D/G and ∞̃_κ : Spec(k) → t^{rs}_{E,D,∞} commutes.
items.note: The bookkeeping needed to descend Theorem 5.14 to a single Hitchin fibre.

items.name: Fibrewise form of the endoscopic description
items.statement: Assume the torsor ∞_{ρ_{E_a}}(k) is non-empty and choose ∞_{ρ_κ} ∈ ρ_{κ,∞}(k) mapping to ∞_ρ. Then the morphism of groupoids µ_{E_a} : M̃^{G-∞,ani}_{H_E,a}(k) → (I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k))_{a,κ} is an equivalence.
items.note: The version used for a fixed point a of the Hitchin base.

items.name: The inclusion of centres Z(X, G) ↪ Z(X, H_E)
items.statement: Since the actions of Out(G) on G and of Out(H_κ) on H_κ preserve the centres, Z(G) = Z(G) ×^{π_0(κ)} ρ_κ and Z(H_E) = Z(H_κ) ×^{π_0(κ)} ρ_κ; property (iii) of Construction 5.2 makes Z(G) ↪ Z(H_κ) equivariant, so twisting by ρ_κ gives Z(G) ↪ Z(H_E) over X and hence Z(X, G) ↪ Z(X, H_E) on Weil restrictions, through which Z(X, G) acts on every section of M̃^{G-∞,ani}_{H_E}.
items.note: The action by which the endoscopic side must be rigidified for the comparison to be an equivalence.

items.name: The G-rigidified endoscopic Higgs stack and µ̄_E
items.statement: M̄^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_{H_E} is the rigidification of M̃^{G-∞,ani}_{H_E} by the action of Z(X, G) ([ACV03, Theorem 5.1.5]); the morphism µ̃_E of Construction 5.9 is Z(X, G)-equivariant and therefore induces µ̄_E : M̄^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_{H_E} → I_µ̂M̄^ani_G.
items.note: Rigidification by the *smaller* centre Z(X, G), not by Z(X, H_E): this asymmetry is what produces the factors |π_0| in Section 6.4.

items.name: The action of Hom(µ̂, Z(X, G))(k) on coendoscopic data
items.statement: On the set of pairs (E, ∞_{ρ_κ}) with E = (κ, ρ_κ, ρ_κ → ρ) a coendoscopic datum for G over k and ∞_{ρ_κ} ∈ ρ_κ(k) above ∞, the group Hom(µ̂, Z(X, G))(k) acts freely: the pair amounts to a homomorphism π_1^ét(X, ∞) → π_0(κ), whose image in Out(G) is Θ = image(π_1^ét(X, ∞) → Out(G)), giving a canonical reduction ρ_{κ,Θ} of ρ_κ to π_0(κ)_Θ = π_0(κ) ×_{Out(G)} Θ; for λ ∈ Hom(µ̂, Z(X, G))(k) = Hom(µ̂, Z(G))(k)^Θ one has π_0(λ·κ)_Θ = π_0(κ)_Θ, so ((λκ, ρ_{κ,Θ}, ρ_{κ,Θ} → ρ), ∞_{ρ_{κ,Θ}}) defines the translated datum, and H_E ≅ H_{λ·E}, giving M̄^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_{H_E} ≅ M̄^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_{H_{λ·E}}.
items.note: The redundancy in the indexing of Theorem 5.14 that must be quotiented out after rigidification.

items.name: Compatible choices of points above infinity
items.statement: A choice of points ∞_ρ ∈ ρ_∞(k) and ∞_{ρ_κ} ∈ ρ_{κ,∞}(k) for all coendoscopic data occurring on I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k) is compatible if for every such E and every λ : µ̂ → Z(G, X) the image of (E, ∞_{ρ_κ}) under λ is again of the form (E', ∞_{ρ_{κ'}}); such a choice exists as soon as all the torsors ρ_{κ,∞} are trivial, since for a non-trivial λ the translated datum E' is necessarily different from E.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Definition 5.21 and Remark 5.22, p. 32
items.note: The hypothesis under which Theorem 5.23 holds.

items.name: The twisted inertia stack of the rigidified Hitchin stack
items.statement: For a compatible choice of points ∞_ρ and ∞_{ρ_κ} for every coendoscopic datum E for G over k occurring on I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k), the resulting morphism of groupoids µ̄_E : ⊔_{{(E,∞_{ρ_κ})}/Hom(µ̂,Z(X,G))(k)} M̄^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_{H_E}(k) → I_µ̂M̄^ani_G(k) is an equivalence.
items.note: The form of the endoscopic description that the p-adic integration of Section 6 uses.

items.name: Fibrewise form for the rigidification
items.statement: Assume ∞_{ρ_{E_a}}(k) ≠ ∅ and choose ∞_{ρ_κ} above ∞_ρ. For a ∈ Ã_G(k) and a fixed type κ there is at most one coendoscopic datum E_a of type κ occurring in the Hitchin fibre (I_µ̂M_G)_a ([Ngô10, Proposition 6.3.3]), and µ_{E_a} : M̄^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_{H_E,a}(k) → (I_µ̂M̄^ani_G(k))_{a,κ} is an equivalence.
items.note: The fibrewise statement used in Lemma 6.8.

items.name: The anisotropic Higgs stack is an algebraic space up to codimension two
items.statement: The stack M̄^ani_G is an algebraic space up to codimension 2.
items.note: Deduced from the description of the twisted inertia stack; it is the hypothesis that lets torsors and line bundles be extended across the non-generic locus in Section 6.5.

items.name: The comparison of regular centralisers
items.statement: For a coendoscopic datum E and c^{G-rs}_E ⊂ c_E the preimage of c^{rs} under ν_E, there is a canonical homomorphism ν_E^*J → J_E over c_E which is an isomorphism over c^{G-rs}_E; it is constructed from the descriptions J^1 = ∏_{ρ_κ×t/c}(ρ_κ × t × T)^{W⋊π_0(κ)} and J_E^1 = ∏_{ρ_κ×t/c_E}(ρ_κ × t × T)^{W_{H_κ}⋊π_0(κ)} and the morphism W ⋊ π_0(κ) → W ⋊ π_0(κ) induced by ι_κ (as in [Ngô10, Proposition 2.5.1]).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Construction 5.26 and Proposition (2.5.1-analogue), pp. 32–33 (equation (20))
items.note: Gives the morphism of Pryms ν_E^*P → P_E along which the two Hitchin systems are compared.

items.name: Compatibility of the endoscopic morphism with the Prym actions
items.statement: Let E be a coendoscopic datum for G over k, S a scheme over A_E, F ∈ M_{H_E}(S) and M ∈ P(S), with E the image of F in M_G(S) and N the image of M in P_E(S). Then there is a canonical isomorphism between the image of F ⊗ N in M_G(S) and E ⊗ M.
items.note: The equivariance that makes the endoscopic description compatible with twisting.

items.name: The rigidified endoscopic Pryms
items.statement: For a coendoscopic datum E and ∞_{ρ_κ} ∈ ρ_κ(k) above ∞: (i) P̃^{G-∞,ani}_E is the pullback of P_E along Ã^{G-∞,ani}_E → A; (ii) Z(X, G) acts on its sections through Z(X, G) → Z(X, H_E) and P̃^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_E is the resulting rigidification; (iii) the action of P_E on M_E induces an action of P̃^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_E on M̄^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_{H_E}; (iv) the morphism ν^*P → P_E is Z(X, G)-equivariant and induces ν̃_E^*P̃ → P̃^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_E; (v) this morphism is compatible with µ̄_E as in Proposition 5.27.
items.note: The transfer of Prym actions across the endoscopic map after rigidification.

items.name: Surjectivity of the transfer of Pryms on fibres
items.statement: For a coendoscopic datum E and ∞_{ρ_κ} ∈ ρ_κ(k) above ∞, and for every point a ∈ Ã^{G-∞,ani,G-rig}_E(k̄), the fibre map P̃_a → P̃_{E,a} of Construction 5.28(iv) is surjective; this follows, as in [Ngô10, 4.17.2], from the fact that J_a → J_{E,a} of Construction 5.26 is generically an isomorphism.
items.note: Used in Lemma 6.7 to compare the component groups of the two Pryms.

items.name: The arithmetic set-up of the proof
items.statement: k is a finite field with q elements, F = k((x)), O = k[[x]]; objects X_k, D_k, G_k, ρ_k, G_k satisfying Situation 4.10 over R = k are fixed together with ∞ ∈ X(k); Situation 6.1 assumes that ρ_∞ splits over Spec k and fixes ∞_ρ ∈ ρ_∞(k), inducing T_∞ ≅ T; X, D, G, ρ, G denote the base changes to O, so that A, M_G, P_G are defined over O with special fibre the original ones; d = deg D is even with d ≥ 2g − 2 (so M̃^ani_G is smooth by [Ngô10, 4.14.1]) and A^♦ ≠ ∅ (for which d > 2g suffices by [Ngô10, 4.7.1]); M̃^ani_G is constant over O and, by [Kre09, Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 5.2] applied to its special fibre, Zariski-locally a finite étale quotient stack, so Theorem 2.21 applies to it.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Situation 6.1 and Section 6, pp. 34–35
items.note: The equal-characteristic local field F = k((x)) is what lets a p-adic integral compute point counts of a variety over k.

items.name: The strong splitting hypothesis
items.statement: Situation 6.2 assumes that all the torsors ρ_{κ,∞} for the coendoscopic data occurring on I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k) (respectively I_µ̂M̃^ani_Ĝ(k)) split; by Remark 5.15 this can be achieved after a finite extension of k, and a compatible choice of splittings is then fixed. For the fundamental lemma this hypothesis is too strong, so in the Geometric Stabilisation Theorem, following Ngô, only the torsor ρ_{κ,∞} of one specific coendoscopic datum is assumed to split.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Situation 6.2 and the paragraph after it, p. 34
items.note: Isolates the hypothesis of Corollary 6.18, which is precisely the one used in [Ngô10, 8.6.3].

items.name: The Π-spaces of the Hitchin system
items.statement: Π ⊂ π_0(P̄_G) is the image of the subgroup X_*(T̂/Z(X, Ĝ)) under the surjection Ã × X_*(T̂) ↠ π_0(P̄_G) of Proposition 4.38, P^Π_G = P̄_G ×_{π_0(P̄_G)} Π, and, after fixing a square root D' of D with Kostant section ε : Ã → M̄_G, M^Π_G ⊂ M̄_G is the closure of the P^Π_G-translate of ε.
items.note: Remark 6.3: the point of the Π-spaces is that π_0(P̃^Π_G|_{A^♦}) = 0 ([Ngô10, Corollaire 4.10.4]), so over A^♦ the Π-Prym is a family of abelian varieties and Proposition 2.2 applies.

items.name: The endoscopic Π-spaces
items.statement: M̄^Π_{H_E} ⊂ M̄^G_{H_E} is the maximal open substack (a union of connected components) for which the square formed by M̄^Π_{H_E} → I_µ̂M̄_G, M̄^G_{H_E} →^{µ̄_E} I_µ̂M̄_G commutes; the square root D' induces a Kostant section Ã_E → M̃_{H_E}, and pulling M̄^Π_{H_E} back along P̃_{H_E} → M̄_{H_E} defines P^Π_{H_E}.
items.note: The endoscopic counterpart of the Π-locus, on which the comparison of Corollary 6.12 takes place.

items.name: The two endoscopic Pryms differ by a character group
items.statement: One has a natural inclusion P^Π_{H_E} ⊃ P̄_{H_E} whose quotient agrees with (Z(X, Ĥ_E)/Z(X, Ĝ))^∨, as follows from the commuting square relating X_*(T̂/Z(X, Ĥ_E)) ↪ X_*(T̂/Z(X, Ĝ)) with π_0(P̄_{H_E}) ↪ π_0(P^Π_{H_E}) and from the fact that the connected components of M̃_{H_E} are parametrised by Z(X, Ĥ_E)^∨ and those of M̃_G by Z(X, Ĝ)^∨ ([Ngô10, Corollaire 4.10.4] and [Ngô10, Proposition 4.16.1]).
items.note: Bookkeeping of the discrepancy between the two rigidifications, which reappears as the factor |π_0| in Section 6.4.

items.name: Unramified twists of Hitchin fibres
items.statement: For a base scheme S and t ∈ H^1_ét(S, P̃^Π_{G,a}) with corresponding P̃^Π_{G,a}-torsor T, the twist is the DM stack M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a} = M̄^Π_{G,a} ×^{P̃^Π_{G,a}}_S T = [(M̄^Π_{G,a} × T)/P̃^Π_{G,a}], étale-locally equivalent to M̄^Π_{G,a} → S. By Lang's theorem and Proposition 4.38, H^1(k, P̃^Π_{G,a}) = H^1(k, π_0(P̃^Π_{G,a})) ≅ π_0(P̃^Π_{G,a}), so every t ∈ X_*(T̂/Z(X, Ĝ)) defines such a twist.
items.note: Lang's theorem for connected algebraic groups over a finite field is used here and is not planned by any layer of the atlas.

items.name: Twists and the isotypic decomposition of the cohomology
items.statement: The Fourier transform of the function π_0(P̃^Π_{G,a}) → Q̄_ℓ, t ↦ #M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a}(k) = Tr(Fr_t, H^*_c(M̄^Π_{G,a,k̄}, Q̄_ℓ)) is the function π_0(P̃^Π_{G,a})^* → Q̄_ℓ, χ ↦ Tr(Fr, H^*_c(M̄^Π_{G,a,k̄}, Q̄_ℓ)^χ); in particular the average (1/|π_0(P̃^Π_{G,a})|) Σ_t #M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a}(k) equals Tr(Fr, H^*_c(M̄^Π_{G,a,k̄}, Q̄_ℓ)^{id}), the stable part of the point count. The proof uses that base change to k̄ identifies the twist with M̄^Π_{G,a,k̄}, under which the geometric Frobenius becomes Fr_t = t · Fr, and Tr(Fr_t, H^*_c(·)^χ) = χ(t) · Tr(Fr, H^*_c(·)^χ).
items.note: This is how a family of point counts of twists recovers the individual isotypic components: the discrete Fourier inversion that turns Theorem 6.11 into Corollaries 6.17 and 6.18.

items.name: Point counts of stacks over finite fields
items.statement: For a Deligne–Mumford stack M of finite type over a finite field k, the (stacky) point count satisfies #M(k) = Σ_n (−1)^n tr(Frob_k, H^n_c(M, Q_ℓ)).
items.note: The Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula for Artin stacks. The scheme case is planned as part of the zeta-function API of WeilConjectures WC.1, but the stack case — which is what every count in this paper means — is not planned anywhere.

items.name: Comparison of the component groups of the two Pryms
items.statement: There is a surjective map π_0(P̃^Π_G) ×_{Ã_G} Ã_{H_E} ↠ π_0(P̃^Π_{H_E}) making the square with X_*(T̂/Z(X, Ĝ)) × Ã_{H_E} ↠ π_0(P̃^Π_G) ×_{Ã_G} Ã_{H_E} and X_*(T̂/Z(X, Ĥ_E)) × Ã_{H_E} → π_0(P̃^Π_{H_E}) commute; surjectivity may be checked on geometric fibres, where it follows from the surjectivity of P̃_{G,a} → P̃_{H_E,a} of Lemma 5.29.
items.note: Lets a twist of the G-side be transported to a twist of the endoscopic side.

items.name: Twisted inertia of a twisted Hitchin fibre
items.statement: For every a ∈ Ã_E(k) and every t ∈ π_0(P̃^Π_{G,a}) there is a natural equivalence (I_µ̂M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a}(k))_κ ≅ M̄^{Π,t}_{H_E,a}(k), where the twist on the right is taken along the map of Lemma 6.7; the equivalence is compatible with the automorphisms AJ_G(λ) of M̄_{G,a} and AJ_{H_E}(λ_H) of M̄_{H_E,a} induced by the Abel–Jacobi points of Construction 4.27.
items.note: The twisted version of Corollary 5.24: it is what makes Theorem 6.11 equivalent to the endoscopic identity of Corollary 6.12.

items.name: The characters χ_s on the twisted inertia stack
items.statement: For s ∈ X_*(T/Z(X, G)) the function χ_s : [I_µ̂M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a}(k)] → Q/Z is defined by χ_s ≡ s(κ) on the part [I_µ̂M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a}(k)_κ] indexed by κ ∈ X_*(T̂) ⊗ (Q/Z)_0, and is composed with the specialisation map to give a function on M̄^{Π,t}_{G,U_a}(O)^♮ with values in Q/Z ⊂ C^×.
items.note: The integrand of the comparison: a character of the local Galois group read off from the twisted inertia stack.

items.name: The henselian neighbourhood U_a and its generic points
items.statement: O^h_a denotes the henselisation of O_Ã at a and U_a = Spec(O^h_a); the O-rational points of U_a are the O-points of Ã with special fibre a, and U_a(O)^♭ = U_a(O) ∩ Ã^♦(F); for a U_a-space Y, Y(O)^♭ = Y(O) ×_{U_a(O)} U_a(O)^♭.
items.note: The local base over which the fibrewise integration is carried out.

items.name: The complement of the generic locus is null
items.statement: U_a(O)^♭ = U_a(O) \ (U_a \ U_a^♦)(O_F), and (U_a \ U_a^♦)(O_F) has measure zero for Weil's canonical measure, by Proposition 2.1(a); moreover H^1(O^h_a, P̃^Π_{G,U_a}) ≅ π_0(P̃^Π_{G,a}), so the twists M̄^{Π,t}_{G,U_a} and their twisted inertia stacks are defined over U_a and come with a specialisation map e : M̄^{Π,t}_{G,U_a}(O)^♮ → [I_µ̂M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a}(k)].
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Remark 6.9 and equation (26), p. 37
items.note: Reduces the identity of integrals to the generic locus, where the Prym is abelian.

items.name: The weight function is constant on isotypic parts
items.statement: There is a function F : X_*(T) ⊗ (Q/Z)_0 → Q such that for every κ ∈ X_*(T) ⊗ (Q/Z)_0 one has w|[I_µ̂M̄_G(k)_κ] = F(κ).
items.note: The weight of Definition 2.20 only depends on the endoscopic type; this is what turns the integral identity into a finite identity of weighted character sums.

items.name: The character-sum identity
items.statement: For all a ∈ Ã(k), t ∈ X_*(T̂/Z(X, Ĝ)) and s ∈ X_*(T/Z(X, G)) one has Σ_{y ∈ [I_µ̂M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a}(k)]} χ_s(y) q^{-w(y)} / |Aut_{I_µ̂M̄^{Π,t}_{G,a}(k)}(y)| = Σ_{z ∈ [I_µ̂M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,a}(k)]} χ_t(z) q^{-w(z)} / |Aut_{I_µ̂M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,a}(k)}(z)|.
items.note: The main technical theorem: a symmetric identity between G and Ĝ, deduced from the equality of the two p-adic integrals (29) and proved fibrewise over the Hitchin base.

items.name: Endoscopic form of the character-sum identity
items.statement: In Situation 6.2, for all a ∈ Ã(k), t ∈ X_*(T̂/Z(X, Ĝ)) and s ∈ X_*(T/Z(X, G)), Σ_{(E,∞_{ρ_κ})/Hom(µ̂,Z(X,G))(k)} s(κ) q^{-F(κ)} #M̄^{Π,t}_{H_E,a}(k) = Σ_{(E',∞_{ρ_ν})/Hom(µ̂,Z(X,Ĝ))(k)} t(ν) q^{-F(ν)} #M̄^{Π,s}_{H'_{ν,ρ},a}(k), where E ranges over the coendoscopy data for G occurring on I_µ̂M̃^ani_G(k) and E' over those for Ĝ occurring on I_µ̂M̃^ani_Ĝ(k).
items.note: Theorem 6.11 rewritten through the description of the twisted inertia stack (Theorem 5.23); this is the form from which geometric stabilisation is extracted.

items.name: Gauge forms on the Hitchin system and fibrewise integration
items.statement: Let η_0 be a generating section of Ω^top_Ã. (a) The line bundle Ω^top_{M̄^{reg,t}_G/Ã} on M̄^{reg,t}_G is trivial (because M̄^{reg}_G is a P̄^{reg}_G-torsor, [Ngô10, Proposition 4.16.1]). (b) For a generating section η_1 of Ω^top_{M̄^{reg,t}_G/Ã} there is a unique generating section ω of Ω^top_{M̄^t_G} with ω|_{M̄^{reg,t}_G} = η_0 ∧ η_1 (Hartogs, using that the complement of M̄^{reg} has codimension ≥ 2). (c) For an integrable g : M̄^t_G(O) → C one has ∫_{M̄^t_G(O)} g · vol_{M̄^t_G} = ∫_{Ã(O)} |η_0| ∫_{M̄^t_{G,b}(F)} g · |η_1|.
items.note: The Fubini step that reduces Theorem 6.11 to an identity of fibrewise integrals; it uses [Igu00, Theorem 7.6.1] on the smooth locus and Proposition 2.1(a) to discard the rest.

items.name: Vanishing of the fibrewise integral when a fibre has no rational point
items.statement: Let b ∈ U_a(O)^♭ be such that the fibre M̄^{Π,t}_{G,b} has no F-rational point. Then χ_t|_{M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,b}(F)} is a non-trivial character (up to translation), and hence ∫_{M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,b}(F)} χ_t · |η_1| = 0.
items.note: Proved from Tate duality: the twist corresponds to a gerbe whose Hasse invariant is the character χ_t, and a non-trivial torsor pairs non-trivially.

items.name: Equality of the fibrewise integrals when both fibres have rational points
items.statement: Let b ∈ U_a(O)^♭ be such that both M̄^{Π,t}_{G,b} and M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,b} have F-rational points. Then χ_t|_{M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,b}} = 1 and χ_s|_{M̄^{Π,t}_{G,b}} = 1, and ∫_{M̄^{Π,t}_{G,b}(F)} |ρ^*η_1| = ∫_{M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,b}(F)} |η_1|.
items.note: Generalises [GWZ17, Lemma 6.15]; the equality of integrals is Proposition 2.2 applied to the prime-to-p isogeny P^{♦,Π}_G → P^{♦,Π}_Ĝ of Construction 4.30.

items.name: Proof of the character-sum identity
items.statement: Theorem 6.11 is equivalent to ∫_{M̄^{Π,t}_{G,U_a}(O)} χ_s · vol_G = ∫_{M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,U_a}(O)} χ_t · vol_Ĝ, and by Lemma 6.13 to the fibrewise identity ∫_{M̄^{Π,t}_{G,b}(F)} χ_s |ρ^*η_1| = ∫_{M̄^{Π,s}_{Ĝ,b}(F)} χ_t |η_1| for every b ∈ U_a(O)^♭; the case where one of the fibres has no F-rational point is Lemma 6.14 and the case where both have one is Lemma 6.15.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Proof of Theorem 6.11, pp. 39–40 (equations (29), (31))
items.note: The assembly of the p-adic argument; the identity of integrals is converted into the identity of weighted counts by Theorem 2.21.

items.name: Isotypic point counts and induction
items.statement: Let a finite group Γ act on H^*_c(Y_k̄, Q̄_ℓ) for a k-variety Y, commuting with the Galois action, and write #^κ Y(k) = Tr(Fr, H^*_c(Y, Q̄_ℓ)^κ) for a character κ of Γ, with #^stab = #^{id}. If Y^Π ⊂ Y is a union of connected components whose cohomology is acted on by a subgroup Γ^Π ⊂ Γ with Γ · H^*_c(Y^Π, Q̄_ℓ) = H^*_c(Y, Q̄_ℓ) and dim H^*_c(Y^Π, Q̄_ℓ) = (|Γ|/|Γ^Π|)^{-1} dim H^*_c(Y, Q̄_ℓ), then Ind_{Γ^Π}^Γ H^*_c(Y^Π, Q̄_ℓ) = H^*_c(Y, Q̄_ℓ) and #^{κ|_{Γ^Π}} Y^Π(k) = #^κ Y(k) for every character κ ∈ Γ^*.
items.note: The passage from the Π-spaces back to the full Hitchin fibres.

items.name: Equality of stable point counts for dual groups
items.statement: For every a ∈ Ã(k) one has #^stab M̄_{G,a}(k) = #^stab M̄_{Ĝ,a}(k). The proof sums the identities (27) over all t ∈ π_0(P̃^Π_{G,a}) and s ∈ π_0(P̃^Π_{Ĝ,a}), using that s ↦ s(κ) is a non-trivial character for κ ≠ 1 and that F(1) = dim M̃_G, and then applies Lemma 6.6 and Lemma 6.16.
items.note: This is Theorem 1.3 and the geometric form of Waldspurger's non-standard fundamental lemma; its statement is planned in the atlas, its proof by p-adic integration is not.

items.name: Geometric stabilisation (the isotypic identity)
items.statement: Let E = (λ, ρ_λ, ρ_λ → ρ) be a coendoscopic datum for Ĝ over k for which the torsor ρ_{λ,∞} splits, and write λ also for the image of λ in π_0(P̃_{G,a})^*. For every point a ∈ Ã_E(k) one has #^λ M̄_{G,a}(k) = q^{dim M̃_G − F(λ)} · #^stab M̄_{Ĥ_E,a}(k), where Ĥ_E is the Langlands dual of H_E, that is, an endoscopy group of G.
items.note: Obtained by Fourier inversion (Lemma 6.6) from Corollary 6.12, together with the fact that M̄^G_{H_E} is a gerbe over M̄_{H_E} banded by Z(X, H_E)/Z(X, G) (Remark 1.2) and Lemma 6.16 and Corollary 6.17 applied to H_E.

items.name: The hypothesis matches Ngô's
items.statement: The assumption of Corollary 6.18 is precisely the one used in [Ngô10, 8.6.3] to deduce the fundamental lemma from geometric stabilisation; in loc. cit. it is formulated for the endoscopy group Ĥ_E, which is equivalent to the assumption stated here for the Langlands dual group H_E.
items.note: The interface with Ngô's deduction of the fundamental lemma, which is what ET.3 consumes.

items.name: The weight constant is the dimension defect
items.statement: For a coendoscopy group H_E of G of type κ, with r^G_{H_E}(D) = ½(dim M̃_G − dim M̃_{H_E}), one has dim M̃_G − F(κ) = r^G_{H_E}(D).
items.note: This identifies the exponent produced by the weight function with the exponent in Ngô's statement, and is the last step of the proof of Theorem 1.1.

items.name: Consequences for the direct images over the algebraic closure
items.statement: Base changing to k̄ and using Chebotarev density, the purity of (Rf̃_*Q̄_ℓ)_k̄ (f̃ proper, M̃ and Ã smooth) and its semisimplicity (Decomposition Theorem), the point-count identities imply that the complexes (Rf̃_{G,*}Q̄_ℓ)^stab_k̄ and (Rf̃_{Ĝ,*}Q̄_ℓ)^stab_k̄ are equivalent, and similarly for the λ-isotypic parts in Corollary 6.18; for Waldspurger's non-standard fundamental lemma the point-count version suffices.
items.note: The only place where the Decomposition Theorem appears, and only to upgrade point counts to sheaves; the proof of the fundamental lemma does not use it.

items.name: Torsors over a Beilinson 1-motive and degree-two extensions
items.statement: For a Beilinson 1-motive P over a base scheme S, a torsor T over P^∨ gives a short exact sequence 0 → P^∨ → ⊔_{n∈Z} T^{⊗n} → Z → 0 whose dual is a short exact sequence of abelian group stacks 0 → BG_m → G → P → 0 (using P^{∨∨} ≅ P), i.e. an element of Ext²_S(P, G_m); dualising back gives the inverse construction, and the two are inverse bijections on isomorphism classes (indeed an equivalence of groupoids).
items.note: The dictionary between twists and gerbes that lets the Hasse invariant detect a twist.

items.name: Tate duality for abelian varieties over a local field
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over a non-archimedean local field F, the pairing A(F) × H^1(F, A^∨) → Q/Z sending (x, t) to the Hasse invariant of the gerbe x^*α_t, where α_t ∈ Ext²_F(A, G_m) ≅ Br(A) corresponds to the torsor t, is perfect ([Mil86, I.3.4]).
items.note: A classical arithmetic duality theorem (Milne, Arithmetic Duality Theorems I.3.4). The atlas plans Poitou–Tate duality for finite modules but not the abelian-variety case that this argument needs.

items.name: The torsor T_G on the Hitchin stack
items.statement: There is a T-torsor on M̃_G(X_k) induced by the morphism M̃_G(X_k) → BT obtained from ev_∞ : M_G → [g/G] and the identification Ã = A ×_c t^{rs}, giving M̃_G → [t^{rs}/T] ≅ t^{rs} × B_kT → B_kT; in Situation 6.1 this torsor is denoted T_G → M̃_G, and quotienting by the centre Z(X, G) ⊂ T gives a T/Z(X, G)-torsor on M̄_G, also denoted T_G. For (E, θ, ∞̃) ∈ M̃^ani_G(X_k) the induced map Aut(E, θ) → T is the embedding of Construction 4.36.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Constructions 6.22, Definition 6.23 and Remark 6.24, p. 43
items.note: The geometric origin of the gerbe whose Hasse invariant is the integrand χ_λ.

items.name: The extension of abelian group stacks attached to T_G
items.statement: A morphism of abelian group stacks H → BA gives an extension 1 → A → H̃ → H → 1 with H̃ = H ×_{BA} {1} (the description of morphisms in a derived category by Ext-groups, Hom_{D(C)}(B, A[1]) ≅ Ext_C(B, A)); applied to the morphism P̃_G → Bun_T(C/A) → B_kT coming from the marked point ∞̃ ∈ C^{sm}, this yields the extension 1 → T → T_P → P̃_G → 1.
items.note: The Prym-level avatar of T_G, which is what makes T_G translation invariant.

items.name: Translation invariance and descent of the torsor to twists
items.statement: The action of the Prym P̂_G on M̂_G lifts to an action of T_P on T_G, so for y ∈ P̄_{G,a}(k) with induced automorphism ψ_y of M̄_{G,a} the torsor ψ_y^*T_G is non-canonically isomorphic to T_G; hence T_G descends to a T/Z(X, G)-torsor T^t_G on every unramified twist M̄^t_{G,a}, the obstruction lying in H²_ét(k, T/Z(X, G)) = Br(k) ⊗ X_*(T/Z(X, G)) = 0 and the descent datum being unique because H^1_ét(k, T/Z(X, G)) = H^1_ét(k, G_m) ⊗ X_*(T/Z(X, G)) = 0.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Remark 6.26, Corollary 6.27 and Definition 6.28, p. 43
items.note: Uses the vanishing of the Brauer group and of H^1 with G_m-coefficients over a finite field.

items.name: The Brauer group of a finite field vanishes
items.statement: Br(k) = 0 for a finite field k.
items.note: Tau Ceti proves that the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial (by Wedderburn's little theorem); the identification of Br(k) with H²_ét(k, G_m) is not part of the cited declaration.

items.name: Hilbert 90 over a finite field
items.statement: H^1_ét(k, G_m) = 0 for a field k, so H^1_ét(k, T/Z(X, G)) = H^1_ét(k, G_m) ⊗ X_*(T/Z(X, G)) = 0.
items.note: Mathlib has Noether's Hilbert 90 for a finite Galois extension (groupCohomology.H1ofAutOnUnitsUnique); the profinite/étale statement used here is planned in the Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology roadmap, Layer 9.

items.name: The classifying map of T_G is the Abel–Jacobi map
items.statement: Over A^♦ the equivalence Hom(P^♦_G, BG_m) ≅ P^♦_Ĝ of Theorem 4.28 turns the classifying map P̃^♦_G → BT of T_G into a section of P̃^♦_Ĝ ⊗ X_*(T̂) ≅ Hom(X_*(T̂), P̃^♦_Ĝ), and the resulting map X_*(T̂) → P̃^♦_Ĝ agrees with the map (19) of Construction 4.37.
