The proof computes (AJ^♦_G)^*T_P as the W-equivariantisation of O(λ∞̃) with its tautological +-structure, where ∞̃ ⊂ C̃ is the divisor given by the image of ∞̃ : Ã → C̃.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Lemma 6.29 with equation (34), pp. 43–44
items.note: This is the identification that makes the gerbe correspond, under Tate duality, to the unramified twists.

items.name: Finiteness of the order of T_G on a Hitchin fibre
items.statement: The restriction of the T/Z(X, G)-torsor T_G to a Hitchin fibre M̄_{G,a} is of finite order. This follows from the claim that there is a morphism P̃_Ĝ ⊗ X_*(T/Z(X, G)) → Pic^{T/Z(X,G)}(M̄_G/Ã) such that for a ∈ Ã(k) the torsor T_G|_{M̄_{G,a}} is the image of a k-rational point of P̃_{Ĝ,a}, together with the facts that π_0(P̃_{Ĝ,a}) is torsion and that the identity component is an abelian variety with finitely many k-rational points; the claim uses that M̄_G is a smooth DM stack which is an algebraic space up to codimension 2 (Corollary 5.25), so torsors extend across M̄^♦_G ⊂ M̄_G, and that the Hitchin map is flat ([Ngô10, Corollaire 4.16.4]).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Lemma 6.30 and Claim 6.31, p. 44
items.note: Finite order is what allows Definition 3.12 to convert T_G into a gerbe.

items.name: The gerbes α_a and α_{U_a}
items.statement: α'_a ∈ H²_ét(M̄^t_{G,a}, T/Z(X, G)) is the gerbe induced by the element of H^1_ét(k, H^1_ét(M̄^t_{G,a}, T/Z(X, G))) sending the topological generator 1 ∈ Ẑ ≅ Gal(k̄/k) to [T^t_G]; writing α'_a = α^0_a α^{00}_a with α^0_a of order coprime to p and α^{00}_a of p-power order, and using the proper base change isomorphism H²_ét(M̄_{G,U_a}, µ_N) ≅ H²_ét(M̄_{G,a}, µ_N) for N coprime to p ([AGV64, Exposé XVI]), α_{U_a} ∈ H²_ét(M̄^t_{G,U_a}, µ_N) is the element corresponding to α_a.
items.note: The Brauer class over the henselian base whose Hasse invariant is integrated.

items.name: The Hasse invariant of the gerbe is the character on the inertia stack
items.statement: For x ∈ M̄_{G,U_a}(O)^♮ and λ ∈ X_*(T/Z(X, G)) the Hasse invariant of λ(x_F^*α_{U_a}) ∈ Br(F) equals χ_λ(e(x)). The proof is Corollary 3.14 together with the claim that the function f_{λ(T_G)} : I_µ̂M̄_G(k) → C induced by the G_m-torsor λ(T_G)/M̄_G agrees with χ_λ: a k-point y of I_µ̂M̄_G gives Bµ̂ → M̄_G, whose composition with M̄_G → BG_m classifying λ(T_G) corresponds to the homomorphism µ̂ → G_m given by λ(κ) ∈ (Q/Z)_0, κ being the type attached to y by Theorem 5.23.
items.note: The statement that closes the circle: it identifies the p-adic integrand χ_s ∘ e with the Hasse invariant of a gerbe, so Tate duality can be applied to it.

items.name: Restriction of Pryms along a finite étale cover and its simplicial diagram
items.statement: For f : Y → X a finite étale morphism of smooth proper curves and G/X quasi-split (also written G/Y for its pullback): (a) Res_{Y/X} : P_{G,X} → P_{G,Y} is induced by pullback of J-torsors; (b) iterated base change of f along itself gives an augmented simplicial object Y_• of finite étale X-schemes; (c) pullback of J-torsors gives an augmented co-simplicial object P_X → P_Y ⇉ P_{Y×_XY} ⋯ of strict Picard stacks.
items.note: The set-up for descent and co-descent of Pryms along the cover that splits the outer form.

items.name: Descent for Pryms
items.statement: The augmented co-simplicial diagram of Definition A.1(c) induces an equivalence Res : P_X ≃ |P_{Y_•}|, by faithfully flat descent applied to the surjective étale morphism f : Y → X.
items.note: The easy half; the content of the appendix is the dual statement, co-descent.

items.name: Finite étale covers are trivialised by a finite étale base change
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a surjective finite étale morphism of schemes of finite presentation over Z. Then there exists a finite étale morphism g : Z → X such that Y ×_X Z → Z is a trivial finite étale morphism, i.e. isomorphic to ⊔_{i∈F} Z → Z for a finite set F. The proof is induction on the degree, using that the diagonal Y → Y ×_X Y is open (f étale) and closed (f finite, hence separated), so U = Y ×_X Y \ Y → Y has degree d − 1.
items.note: The elementary input that makes norm maps for étale sheaves well defined.

items.name: Norm maps for étale sheaves of abelian groups
items.statement: Let J be a sheaf of abelian groups on the small étale site of X and f : Y → X a surjective finite étale morphism, and let J_Y = f_*f^{-1}J. (a) If f is trivial, say f ≅ ⊔_{i∈F} X → X, then Nm_{Y/X} : J_Y → J_X is the multiplication map J^F → J, (s_i)_{i∈F} ↦ ∏_{i∈F} s_i. (b) A morphism nm : J_Y → J_X is a norm map if g^*nm = Nm_{Y×_XZ/Z} for every g as in Lemma A.3.
items.note: Norms of étale sheaves are the dual of restriction, and give the simplicial diagram (35).

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of norm maps
items.statement: For f : Y → X, J and J_Y as in Definition A.4 a norm map Nm_{Y/X} : J_Y → J exists and is unique: choose g : Z → X finite étale trivialising f (Lemma A.3); for an étale open h : U → X and s ∈ J_Y(U), the section g^*s ∈ J_Y(U ×_X Z) ≅ J_X(U ×_X Z)^F has components with p_1^*s_i = p_2^*s_i, so the product ∏_{i∈F} s_i satisfies the same descent condition and descends to Nm_{Y/X}(s) ∈ J(U), independently of g.
items.note: Together with Definition A.4 this gives the augmented simplicial diagram (35) of étale sheaves.

items.name: Local co-descent
items.statement: The augmented simplicial diagram J ← J_Y ⇇ J_{Y×_XY} ⋯ of (35) is a limit diagram in the category of sheaves of abelian groups on the small étale site of X, that is J ≃ |J_{Y_•}|; moreover this holds in the derived ∞-category of étale sheaves of abelian groups. The proof reduces étale-locally to a trivial covering ⊔_{i∈F} X → X and then, by the Dold–Kan correspondence, to the computation that the chain complex J^F_X ← J^{F×F}_X ← ⋯ with the alternating sum of the face maps ∂_{n,i}g(c_0,…,c_{n-1}) = ∏_{c∈F} g(c_0,…,c_{i-1},c,c_i,…) has vanishing homology in positive degrees and J_X in degree 0.
items.note: The technical heart of the appendix.

items.name: The Dold–Kan correspondence
items.statement: For an abelian category A the normalised chain complex functor is an equivalence SimplicialObject(A) ≃ ChainComplex(A, N).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Lemma A.6, proof, p. 47 ([Sta, Tag 019D])
items.note: Mathlib has the Dold–Kan equivalence for abelian categories (and for idempotent-complete preadditive ones).

items.name: Deligne's description of strict Picard stacks
items.statement: The homotopy category of strict Picard stacks, obtained by identifying 2-isomorphic 1-morphisms, is equivalent to the derived category of complexes of abelian sheaves concentrated in degrees [−1, 0] ([AGV64, XVIII.1.4]); with respect to this equivalence one has P ≃ RΓ(X_S, J[1]).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Section A.1 and Remark A.7, p. 48
items.note: The derived-category model in which co-descent for the Prym is proved.

items.name: Global co-descent for Pryms
items.statement: For a finite étale morphism Y → X of smooth proper curves the norm maps Nm_{Y/X} : P_Y → P_X give an augmented simplicial object of strict Picard stacks whose augmentation is an equivalence P_G(X)(S) ≃ |P_G(Y_•)(S)|. The proof uses Lemma A.6 together with the fact that Rπ_* commutes with the relevant small coproducts and colimits, reduced to uniformly bounded-below complexes by truncation.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Corollary A.9 and Definition A.8, p. 48
items.note: The dual of Lemma A.2, and the statement that makes the duality descend to outer forms.

items.name: Donagi–Pantev and Chen–Zhu duality in the split case
items.statement: Let G/k be a split reductive group scheme with char(k) = 0 or |W| not divisible by char(k), and Ĝ its Langlands dual; for X/k a smooth projective curve there is an isomorphism A_G ≅ A_Ĝ mapping A^♦_G to A^♦_Ĝ, with respect to which the abelian group stacks P_G and P_Ĝ are dual: AJ^* : P_G ≅ P̂_G.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.06739v2 (28 October 2019), Theorem A.10, p. 49 ([DP12, Theorem A], [CZ17, Theorem 1.2.1])
items.note: The input to the quasi-split case; it is itself not planned anywhere in the atlas.

items.name: Restriction and norm are dual
items.statement: For f : Y → X finite étale, Res^∨_{Y/X} = Nm_{Y/X} : P_{G,X} → P_{G,Y}, i.e. the square formed by AJ^* : P_{G,X} ≅ P^∨_{Ĝ,X}, Res_{Y/X} and Nm^∨_{Y/X} commutes. This follows from the commutativity of the square relating AJ_Y : C_Y × X_*(T̂) → P_{Ĝ,Y} and AJ_X : C_X × X_*(T̂) → P_{Ĝ,X}, since the norm of the W-equivariantisation of O_{C_Y}(λy) is the W-equivariantisation of O_{C_X}(λf(y)).
items.note: The compatibility that lets descent on one side be matched with co-descent on the other.

items.name: Duality of Pryms for quasi-split group schemes
items.statement: Let X/k be a smooth projective curve over a field k and G/X a quasi-split reductive group scheme, an outer form of a split reductive G/k, with char(k) = 0 or |W| not divisible by char(k). Then A_G ≅ A_Ĝ maps A^♦_G to A^♦_Ĝ and, with respect to this identification, the Beilinson 1-motives P_G and P_Ĝ are dual. The proof takes f : Y → X finite étale trivialising the outer form (Lemma 4.8), puts the co-descent diagram for P^∨ and the descent diagram for P̂ side by side, and uses that AJ^* is an equivalence at every level (Theorem A.10) together with Corollary A.9 and Lemma A.2.
items.note: The general form of Theorem 4.28; it is the duality that Lemmas 6.14–6.15 apply fibrewise.
